question.leadin: Identify some people in the history of a certain empire that was neither holy nor Roman.
question.text: This Holy Roman Emperor, third of the Salian dynasty, was involved in the Investiture Controversy with the Papacy and stood in the snow for three days begging for forgiveness.
question.clue: This monarch defeated the first Percy rebellion at the Battle of Shrewsbury, which saw the death of Hotspur.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Luebeck ended the Danish involvement in this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict that began with the Bohemian Revolt and the Defenestration of Prague and primarily pitted the Hapsburgs and their allies against the Bourbons and their allies.
swap.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

question.leadin: After this ruler won the 1159 Siege of Crema, he attempted to boss around the future pope Alexander III. Alexander's refusal led this man to support Victor IV in his bid to be pope.
question.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor that was excommunicated by Alexander III.
question.clue: This man journeyed with Phillip II Augustus after taking up the cross at the Diet of Mainz.

swap.leadin: A pre-Protestant Christian group named for this man prompted a series of namesake Bohemian wars that lasted from 1419 to 1433.
swap.text: Name this Bohemian priest, who was an advocate of realism in the Catholic Church and was a strong proponent of John Wycliffe, whose writings were first banned by Pope Innocent VII ["the seventh"].
swap.clue: This man's teachings were heavily influenced by those of John Wycliffe, although because of this he was convicted of heresy and burned at the stake at the Council of Constance.

question.leadin: Answer some questions about the Battle of Wimpfen.
question.text: The attackers in the Battle of Wimpfen belonged to this organization that opposed the Protestant Union. A French organization founded by Henry, Duke of Guise was also named this two-word phrase.
question.clue: Another group of this name opposed King Henry III and took power during the Day of the Barricades.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Thirty Years' War.
swap.text: The Bohemian period of the Thirty Years' War was ended by this 1620 battle near Prague, in which the Count of Tilly defeated Protestant forces lead by Christian of Anhalt.
swap.clue: Descartes may have been present at this one-hour battle, as an observer in the army of the count of Bucquoy.

question.text: The first king of newly independent Greece was a Bavarian prince of this name. A Prussian politician with this first name kept power by making melodramatic offers to resign, which persuaded Wilhelm I to retain him.
question.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

swap.leadin: 27 leaders of one revolt named for this historic region were executed in the Old Town Square of its capital.
swap.text: Name this historic region in which Protestants revolted against Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II in 1618. That revolt began after two of the emperor's representatives were defenestrated in this historic region's capital.
swap.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

question.text: In 1535, Suleiman lost Tunis to this Holy Roman Emperor, the son of Philip I and Joanna of Castille.
question.clue: This ruler's forces sacked Rome while fighting against the League of Cognac, and later captured Francis I after winning the Battle of Pavia.

swap.leadin: This man may have helped complete Odo of Metz's designs for a palace in Aachen, and he once dispatched a servant to pilfer holy remains from Rome to increase the piety of churches he founded.
swap.text: Identify this colleague of Alcuin, a preeminent Frankish biographer from the eighth and ninth centuries.
swap.clue: The preface to this notoriously short man's most famous work was written by Walafrid Strabo.

question.text: The First Defenestration led to this series of wars, in which the followers of an eponymous heretic, commanded by Jan Zizka, defeated King Sigismund at Vitkov Hill.
question.clue: Raids called "beautiful rides" were conducted by Prokop the Great in this conflict, which ended at the Battle of Lipany where the Utraquists defeated the Taborites.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about times when people were chucked out of windows in Prague.
swap.text: The First Defenestration of Prague in 1419, which killed seven Prague town council members, was carried out by members of this religious movement, who followed the teachings of a heretic burned at the Council of Constance.
swap.clue: These people, led by Jan Zelivsky, threw Catholic magistrates out of a window during the First Defenestration of Prague.

question.leadin: As a result of declarations made at this event, Jacob Poost was arrested, while Jan van Essen and Hendrik Vos were burnt at the stake.
question.text: Name this event condemning a man who defended his views from Leo X's ("the tenthʼs") bull Exsurge domine. Johann Eck presided over this event, during which its central participant may have said "Here I stand, I cannot do otherwise."
question.clue: One prominent participant in this meeting had to hide at the Wartburg at its conclusion.

swap.text: The Falun mine was initially outpaced by production at the mines at Rammelsberg. Those mines were first discovered during the reign of this ruler, and were described in the chronicle of his advisor Widukind of Corvey.
swap.answerHtml: Otto the Great [or Otto I, Holy Roman Emperor; or Otto der Grosse; prompt on Otto]
swap.clue: He subjugated Berengar of Ivrea to rescue the kidnapped Adelaide, whom he married, making him King of Lombardy.

question.text: This league defeated at the Battle of Muhlberg was a militarized version of the earlier League of Torgau and was composed of Lutheran German princes who opposed Charles V.
question.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

swap.text: Earlier, in 1629, Ferdinand II had tried to enforce the "Ecclesiastical Reservation" of the Peace of Augsburg by issuing this edict.
swap.clue: Maximilian von Trautmannsdorf's Points of Pirna attempted to reconcile one party who had been alienated by this declaration, which was defended vociferously in Paul Laymann's Pacis Composito.

question.leadin: The foremost early leader of this faction was Jacob of Mies, who preached at the University of Prague that the laity should receive the Eucharist in both bread and wine.
question.text: Name this moderate faction that maintained amicable relations with the Roman Catholic Church, and emerged victorious over their rivals at the Battle of Lipany during the Hussite Wars.
question.clue: The radical Taborites were opposed by this more moderate Hussite faction, who eventually broke with their brethren and fought on the side of the Catholics.

swap.leadin: John of Bohemia, of Crecy fame, originally gave Charles IV this name, but Charles renamed himself in honor of Charles the Fair of France.
swap.text: Give this name of several rulers of Prague, like Charles' Nepomuk-killing son. A beloved duke of this name was murdered by his not-so-good brother, Boleslaus the Cruel.
swap.clue: This name was borne by the protege of Saint Ludmila who was killed after refusing to fight Henry the Fowler.

question.leadin: Name the following battles of Gustavus Adolphus FTPE.
question.text: In this 1631 battle, Adolphus led the Protestant forces to their first victory in the Thirty Years War.
question.clue: Another cavalry charge by Furstenberg drove off John George I and his Saxon troops, exposing the eventual victor's left flank.

swap.leadin: This man was made a saint and posthumously declared the king of the Czechs after his death.
swap.text: Name this knize and saint who was supposedly murdered by his brother, Boleslav the Cruel, in 935 CE.
swap.answerHtml: Wenceslas I [or Wenceslaus I; or Saint Wenceslas; or Good King Wenceslas; prompt on “Wenceslas”]
swap.clue: This son of Dragomir, the prince and patron saint of Bohemia.
